issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal differs between the problem statement/solution and the template. The UML and solution expect Meal(String, String[]), and the Main example constructs Meal with (String name, String[] ingredients). However, the template's Meal constructor is declared as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion when students follow the problem text and Main examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's Meal constructor signature to match the UML/problem and solution: change the constructor to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so it aligns with the Main examples and the intended design.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect the Meal constructor signature to be Meal(String, String[]) (name first, ingredients second), but the template's Meal class defines the constructor with the parameters reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This signature mismatch creates confusion for students because the example code in Main and the UML both use Meal(name, ingredients), while the template requires the opposite ordering, potentially causing compilation errors or incorrect usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the template Meal class to match the problem statement and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) { ... }. Also ensure the example usage in Main and any documentation match this parameter order.
